Yes — F-12 is strongly connected to injectors F-5 (0.2922) and F-4 (0.2684), both >0.2, so injected-water arrival is a real risk.

F-14's WCT_SEVERE alert (A_WCT_SEVERE_F-14_2016-07-01) was triggered by the water_cut reading R_water_cut_F-14_2016-07-01 = 0.9662 (~96.6%) on 2016-07-01; the recommended intervention is I_WCT_SEVERE_F-14_2016-07-01 (polymer_injection, $11.44/bbl, +8,686 bbl).

The earliest water-breakthrough alerts were both raised on 2010-06-01 — a tie between wells F-12 and F-14. F-12's alert (A_WATER_BREAKTHROUGH_F-12_2010-06-01) was triggered by its water_cut reading of 0.5446 (R_water_cut_F-12_2010-06-01), with recommended intervention polymer_injection (I_WATER_BREAKTHROUGH_F-12_2010-06-01). F-14's alert (A_WATER_BREAKTHROUGH_F-14_2010-06-01) was triggered by its water_cut reading of 0.5619 (R_water_cut_F-14_2010-06-01), with recommended intervention gas_lift_opt (I_WATER_BREAKTHROUGH_F-14_2010-06-01).

F-5→F-11 is the dominant flow path from injector F-5, with the highest connectivity weight (0.4368, vs 0.2922/0.0803/0.0728 for its other producers) and a short 45-day transit lag. So a large share of injected water reaches F-11 fast, driving early breakthrough — confirmed by F-11's WATER_BREAKTHROUGH alert (2015-08-01) and subsequent HIGH_WOR alerts.

The cheapest intervention is I_WCT_SEVERE_F-14_2015-05-01 (est_cost_per_bbl = 8.28, well 15/9-F-14). Provenance chain: I_WCT_SEVERE_F-14_2015-05-01 —RECOMMENDED_FOR→ Alert A_WCT_SEVERE_F-14_2015-05-01 (WCT_SEVERE) —TRIGGERED_BY→ MetricReading R_water_cut_F-14_2015-05-01 —MEASURED_BY→ source sensor S_water_cut_F-14. (The intervention is also FOLLOWED_BY the outcome reading R_np_cum_F-14_2016-09-01.)

A HIGH_WOR alert is supported by a `log_wor` MetricReading crossing the threshold log_wor ≥ 0 (i.e., WOR ≥ 1, water rate ≥ oil rate). Example: alert A_HIGH_WOR_F-12_2010-06-01 is TRIGGERED_BY reading R_log_wor_F-12_2010-06-01 with value 0.0778 (log10), the first month above 0 (the prior reading R_log_wor_F-12_2010-05-01 was -0.0153, below threshold).

F-12: early but gradual/smooth breakthrough — negligible (<3%) through 2009, then a steady monotonic climb from late-2009 reaching ~49% (May 2010), ~65% (Aug 2010), ~76% (mid-2011). F-15 D: dry (0%) into late-2014, low plateau (~3–8%) to mid-2015, then an abrupt step-change breakthrough (~7.6% Jul-2015 → ~34% Aug-2015), rising to ~56% (Jan-2016) and ~61% (mid-2016). Difference: F-12 = slow gradual S-curve; F-15 D = long dry period then sudden sharp water breakthrough.

F-5 supports F-11 more strongly because its INJECTS_INTO weight is higher (0.4368) than F-4's weight (0.3473). Both have the same lag (tau_days = 45), so with equal injection timing, a larger fraction of F-5's injected water reaches F-11, meaning stronger pressure/support connectivity than the F-4→F-11 path.

Highest-risk producer = F-12 (W_F-12), flagged by 92 alerts (WATER_BREAKTHROUGH 2010-06 escalating to sustained WCT_SEVERE from 2013-03), confirmed by latest water_cut 0.8835. Root cause is injector-driven water from W_F-5 (weight 0.2922) and W_F-4 (weight 0.2684). Best recommendation by uplift-per-cost is I_WCT_SEVERE_F-12_2014-02-01 (rate_reduction, 10,323.9 bbl @ $8.49/bbl, ratio ≈1216), then water_shutoff I_WCT_SEVERE_F-12_2013-03-01.

Every node stores a source_record_id (e.g., Well W_F-12 → volve:well:15/9-F-12; Alert A_WCT_SEVERE_F-12_2013-03-01 → rule:WCT_SEVERE:R_water_cut_F-12_2013-03-01) as a provenance link to the originating upstream record. This matters because citation validation can verify each cited id resolves to a real, source-backed node and reject fabricated/unsupported ids, making answers auditable against ground truth.

The recommended water_shutoff interventions are caused by water-cut (WCT) diagnostics: each intervention is RECOMMENDED_FOR an Alert that is TRIGGERED_BY a high water_cut MetricReading. F-12 and F-14 shutoffs stem from WCT_SEVERE alerts (high water cut, e.g. F-12 water_cut=0.9006 frac), and the F-15 D shutoff stems from a WATER_BREAKTHROUGH alert — in every case the trigger is the water_cut metric crossing the alert threshold.
F-4 injects into 4 producers: F-11 (w=0.3473), F-12 (w=0.2684), F-14 (w=0.1628), F-1C (w=0.1401); F-11 is the strongest, F-1C the weakest (all tau=45 days).

The three node types form a chain centered on the Alert. (1) A MetricReading (e.g. R_water_cut_F-12_2013-03-01, a water_cut sample) is the triggering reading — the Alert points to it via an outgoing TRIGGERED_BY edge (Alert)-[:TRIGGERED_BY]->(MetricReading). (2) That reading itself is attributed to a sensor/well series via (MetricReading)-[:MEASURED_BY]->(Series, e.g. S_water_cut_F-12), and both the Alert and reading carry the same well (15/9-F-12). (3) The recommended Intervention (e.g. I_WCT_SEVERE_F-12_2013-03-01) links to the Alert via (Intervention)-[:RECOMMENDED_FOR]->(Alert), and can in turn point to a later outcome reading via (Intervention)-[:FOLLOWED_BY]->(MetricReading, e.g. R_np_cum_F-12_2016-09-01). So: MetricReading <-TRIGGERED_BY- Alert <-RECOMMENDED_FOR- Intervention -FOLLOWED_BY-> outcome MetricReading.
